summary.text: A 55-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes, diverticulitis and hyperlipidemia, whose home medications included insulin, canagliflozin, metformin and others, presented to the emergency room on April 12, 2020 with anorexia, cough and shortness of breath after a seven-day history of cough, fever, myalgia and malaise. His baseline serum creatinine was 1.24 mg/dl.

In the emergency department he was afebrile but tachycardic, tachypneic and hypoxic at 85% on room air, with an arterial pH of 7.11, positive ketonuria and lactic acid 4.2 mmol/L, consistent with diabetic ketoacidosis. Creatinine was 2.96 mg/dL with hematuria and proteinuria, potassium 7 mmol/L, elevated inflammatory markers and mild patchy bilateral opacities on chest X-ray. COVID-19 testing was positive.

He was intubated for hypoxia, admitted to the intensive care unit and given norepinephrine, insulin and antibiotics. CRRT began on hospital day two, with convalescent plasma on days six and nine and dexamethasone for eight days. CRRT stopped on day 19 and hemodialysis began on day 20. Tracheostomy followed on day 24, ventilator weaning on day 30, and a venous thrombosis on day 33 treated with heparin then coumadin.

Repeat COVID-19 tests from day 32 were all negative. He remained oliguric until before day 42, then made good urine output, received his last hemodialysis on day 45, and by day 48 the AKI had resolved and renal function was reported to have returned to normal. He was discharged to sub-acute rehabilitation after 48 days in hospital.

ambiguities.issue: The ED sentence prints arterial PCO_(2) twice with different values (16 and 66) and also "PCO_(2) total arterial 6", with no units; this is a source conflict. Neither value is stored as an accepted result.

evidence.quote: partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PCO_(2)) arterial 16

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide which arterial PCO2 is correct or reinterpret the 66 as an oxygen value; do not interpret the total value.

ambiguities.issue: Day 48 serum creatinine is printed as 1.30 mg/dL in the text and 1.38 in Table 1 (one-character discrepancy). Both are held as review-only.

evidence.quote: serum creatinine level improved to 1.30 mg/dL

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not choose either value as the day 48 creatinine.

ambiguities.issue: Text and Table 1 report the same admission panel ("Initial blood and urinary examination are shown in Table 1") with different unit labels. Ferritin 2951 is ng/mL in the text and mg/liter in the table, and procalcitonin 4.31 is mg/ml in the text while the table row states a ng /ml reference interval: these are source conflicts and both sides are review-only. LDH 501 is IU/L in the text and U/liter in the table, the same unit spelled differently, so it is one item citing both.

evidence.quote: Inflammatory markers were elevated (lactate dehydrogenase level 501 IU/L, C reactive protein 32.7 mg/L, ferritin level 2951 ng/mL, and procalcitonin level 4.31 mg/ml).

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not correct or convert the ferritin or procalcitonin units or choose either label as the true one.

ambiguities.issue: The ED text values for blood glucose (559 mg/dL), lactic acid (4.2 mmol/L), positive ketonuria and bicarbonate/HCO3 are not stated to be the same measurements as the Table 1 "On admission" glucose (525), lactic acid (4.2), urine ketones (positive +2) and carbon dioxide (8) cells, so they are kept as separate facts.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not merge or reconcile ED and table values; do not conclude the differing glucose values are an error.

ambiguities.issue: The repeat COVID-19 testing sentence says the test was repeated for the next two days and all tests were negative; the exact number and dates of tests are not stated.

evidence.quote: He was tested for COVID 19 again on day 32 and test was repeated for next two days, all tests came back negative.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer the number of negative tests or their calendar dates.

ambiguities.issue: Units and labels in Table 1 are kept as printed even where they look inconsistent (White cells "per ml" with single-digit values; Platelets with no unit; ferritin "mg/liter"). No flags were derived from the reference ranges.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not rescale or add units.

ambiguities.issue: Home medications are listed without stating whether they were being taken at the time of the presentation or their dosing basis (for example "16 units" Humalog before meal and bedtime).

evidence.quote: Home medications included atorvastatin, clomiphene, insulin Humalog 16 units subcutaneous before meal and bedtime, canagliflozin, Levemir, 54 units subcutaneous daily, lisinopril, and metformin.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer current use or a per-dose versus daily dose for the insulins.

article_limitations: The article lists no figures and no supplements; no visual, figure-EHR or privacy sidecars apply.
The ED arterial blood gas sentence prints PCO_(2) arterial as both 16 and 66 (source conflict) and a total value of 6; none is accepted.
Day 48 creatinine differs between text (1.30) and Table 1 (1.38); both are review-only.

Ferritin and procalcitonin admission values carry incompatible units between text and Table 1 (source conflicts, both sides review-only); LDH IU/L vs U/liter is one item. Table 1 units are kept as printed (including odd labels such as White cells per ml).
The Table 1 Events row (CRRT, Off CRRT, HD, Last HD under Hospital Day 2/19/20/45) agrees with the hospital days stated in the text; the text sentences are cited for ordering.
Discussion paragraphs mostly describe published literature; only explicit index-patient sentences were used.
No flags were derived from Table 1 reference ranges; high flags come only from text that calls a value elevated, tachycardic, tachypneic, hypoxic or hypotensive.
